author: reek
body: Volcano-style query executor. Walks the RelOp tree and materializes results. Each operator produces a list of rows. Future optimization: streaming iterators instead of full materialization.

author: reek
body: A left outer join emits one row per MATCHING PAIR, exactly as the inner join does, and falls back to a single null-padded row only for a left row that matches nothing. It does not emit one row per left row: this loop used to take the FIRST match and move on, so a left join whose predicate admits several right rows silently lost all but one of them (three left rows against ten right rows under an always-true predicate answered 3 where a join answers 30). exec-join-inner already collects every match for one left row, so the two joins now agree by construction.

author: reek
body: The row count is snapshotted into `before` on purpose. exec-join-inner accumulates with list-push, which writes in place and hands back the SAME list, so after the call `grown` and `acc` are one object and comparing their lengths to each other always says "equal" -- every left row would then also collect a null-padded row. The count has to be taken before the call, not derived from the two names afterwards.

author: reek
body: Both children evaluate to full row lists and the hash join does the matching: the right side is the build input, the left side probes. The join keys are the column lists paired positionally, hashed as one composite key per row. The hash join emits probe values before build values, therefore the merged rows carry the left side's columns first and the merged schema mirrors the nested-loop join's left-then-right order. Duplicate column names survive the merge and a lookup by name finds the left occurrence, in the same manner as the other joins.
